standing.title: NYC Resistor Public Craft Night
standing.description: Open craft night at the NYC Resistor hacker collective: bring a project, use the space, meet members. Free and open to the public, 18 and over.
standing.time_note: Mondays and Thursdays 6:30-9:30pm. Free, but 18+ only.
standing.practical_note: Fourth-floor walkup; confirm on Eventbrite since craft night is occasionally cancelled for private classes.
standing.date_idea_reason: A free, hands-on makerspace evening is an unusual low-cost date with something to actually do.
standing.why_now: Runs twice a week year-round and is one of the few genuinely free weeknight drop-in activities.

standing.title: Whitney Museum free Friday evening
standing.description: The Whitney is free to all every Friday evening from 5 to 10pm, and also on the second Sunday of each month.
standing.time_note: Free admission Fridays 5-10pm. Free tickets are limited and released in advance.
standing.practical_note: Reserve the free timed ticket ahead; walk-up availability runs out on busy evenings.
standing.date_idea_reason: Free evening museum hours next to the High Line and a dense stretch of bars, so the museum is the anchor rather than the whole plan.
standing.why_now: A standing free window that makes a good anchor for a Friday evening in the Meatpacking District.

standing.title: MoMA free Friday evening
standing.description: MoMA offers free admission on Friday evenings. Free tickets are limited, released in advance, and go quickly.
standing.time_note: Free Friday evenings, roughly 4-8pm. Confirm the current window and ticket release on moma.org.
standing.practical_note: Book the free timed ticket the moment it is released; the line for walk-ups is long.
standing.why_now: A standing weekly free window at a museum that is otherwise one of the most expensive in the city.

holiday_plan.intro: Thanksgiving falls on Thursday; a four-day weekend requires Friday, November 27 off, so confirm your own work schedule. Choose one escape rather than combining these destinations. Options stay within roughly a three-hour normal-traffic drive of NYC, with Longwood near the outer edge; holiday traffic can take longer. Research checked November 15, 2026.

trips.title: Beacon: contemporary art, with a holiday-hours caveat
trips.why: Dia's large-scale contemporary art in a former factory makes a strong indoor anchor, followed by Main Street browsing and food. Keep this conditional rather than treating museum access as confirmed.
trips.transport: Car-free: Metro-North Hudson Line from Grand Central to Beacon, then walk to Dia and town.
trips.time_budget: A full day, allowing substantial gallery time and walking between the station, museum and Main Street.
trips.booking_note: Aim for November 27–29 only after confirming Dia's holiday hours and admission or timed-entry requirements. Dia's official pages returned 403 errors; neither holiday opening nor ticket availability was verified. Cold Spring is the better-supported substitute.

trips.title: Cold Spring: foundry ruins, woodland and river views
trips.why: Combine West Point Foundry Preserve's industrial history and woodland paths with the waterfront and Main Street. This provides a nature-and-culture outing without relying on a seasonal house tour or strenuous summit hike.
trips.transport: Car-free: Metro-North Hudson Line from Grand Central to Cold Spring; continue on foot.
trips.time_budget: An unhurried day trip; complete the preserve walk before dusk.
trips.booking_note: Scenic Hudson confirms the preserve is free and open year-round, dawn to dusk. Check park alerts and walking conditions, and confirm individual restaurant and shop holiday hours. MTA has published a separate November 26 timetable; do not assume Friday uses Thursday's service.

trips.title: Hudson: a makers' market and one-night food escape
trips.why: Basilica Farm & Flea brings regional makers, vintage goods and locally sourced food into a reused waterfront factory. Pair it with Warren Street browsing and dinner; November 27–28 or 28–29 works within the confirmed market dates.
trips.transport: Car-free: Amtrak from New York Penn/Moynihan to Hudson, then walking. Choose lodging in the downtown area rather than an outlying countryside property.
trips.time_budget: One night and two partial days, with the market anchoring one daytime block.
trips.booking_note: The organizer confirms November 27–29, 10 a.m.–5 p.m. each day, and links to admission tickets. Check market admission, both train journeys, lodging and dinner separately. Amtrak pages were blocked, so date-specific service, fares and seats remain unconfirmed.

trips.title: Old Westbury: estate architecture and late-autumn gardens
trips.destination: Old Westbury, Long Island, New York
trips.why: Westbury House and its designed landscape offer an architecture-and-nature alternative to another Hudson Valley trip. Its published weekend schedule makes this a useful replacement for unverified Storm King access.
trips.transport: Car-required for this proposed itinerary: drive to the visitor entrance at 71 Old Westbury Road.
trips.time_budget: A daylight outing with time for both the house and grounds.
trips.booking_note: Choose November 28 or 29. The published November–December schedule is weekends only, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; November 26–27 are closed under that schedule. Nonmember final admission is 3 p.m. Advance online tickets are required except for members and library-pass holders. No holiday illumination event is assumed.

trips.title: Philadelphia: holiday market and a major art exhibition
trips.why: Combine Christmas Village's craft and food stalls with the Philadelphia Museum of Art's Marcel Duchamp exhibition, listed through January 31, 2027. Staying November 27–28 or 28–29 gives both activities room.
trips.transport: Car-free: NJ TRANSIT Northeast Corridor from New York Penn to Trenton, then SEPTA Trenton Line to Philadelphia. Use walking and SEPTA locally.
trips.time_budget: One night; allow a substantial travel block each way because the rail itinerary requires a transfer.
trips.booking_note: Christmas Village confirms November 26 hours of 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; Friday–Saturday noon–9 p.m. and Sunday noon–8 p.m. Museum regular hours support Friday–Sunday visits, but its November 26 holiday exception was not established. Check exhibition admission, hotel terms and both operators' date-specific schedules.

trips.title: Longwood: cosmic Christmas displays and an overnight
trips.destination: Kennett Square and Longwood Gardens, Pennsylvania
trips.why: The confirmed 2026 display combines astronomy-inspired conservatory installations with outdoor lights. A nearby overnight avoids building the outing around a late return drive.
trips.transport: Car-required for this proposed gardens-and-local-lodging itinerary. Longwood also lists direct OurBus service from NYC, but operating dates and return trips for this weekend were not verified.
trips.time_budget: One night. Longwood recommends 3.5–4 hours in the gardens and lists NYC as 130 miles away; this is the outer-edge driving choice.
trips.booking_note: The event runs November 20–January 10, with published daily hours of 10 a.m.–11 p.m. Obtain a timed ticket before arranging the overnight; most members also need reservations. November 27–29 are blackout dates for complimentary admission tickets. Dining reservations are separate. No ticket or room availability was checked.

local_ideas.title: NYBG Holiday Train Show after dark
local_ideas.why: Car-free Bronx option: botanical models of NYC landmarks and model trains, with explicitly confirmed extended evenings on all three dates. The Conservatory stays open until 8 p.m., last entry 7:15 p.m.; evening programming includes live jazz. Select the appropriate exhibition ticket.

local_ideas.title: Bryant Park Winter Village: skating, shops and a Santa option
local_ideas.why: Car-free Midtown outing with confirmed 2026 seasonal dates. Skating admission is free, but rentals cost extra and skating requires a reservation. Club Santa is separately ticketed on November 28–29. The tree lighting is December 1, outside this planning window.

items.title: Brasserie Boulud's new Lincoln Square restaurant
items.summary: Daniel Boulud's consolidated brasserie replaces the former Bar Boulud, Boulud Sud and Épicerie arrangement. The current dinner menu offers both relatively accessible brasserie dishes and larger seafood orders.
items.price_text: Burger Classique $25; boudin blanc $25; trout $30; coq au vin $36; six-ounce filet mignon steak frites $48.
items.conditions: These are ordinary menu prices, not a special offer. Earlier all-day-service plans are not treated as current hours. Booking availability and holiday exceptions are unknown.
items.verification_note: The official current menu confirms these prices and Tuesday–Sunday 4:30–10:30pm service. The $25 burger is the Burger Classique; the separately named Brasserie Boulud Burger is $29. Source: https://www.brasserieboulud.com/our-menu/daily-menu. October 8 was announced in https://ny.eater.com/restaurant-openings/414137/brasserie-boulud-nyc-restaurant-opens-daniel-boulud-lincoln-center-upper-west-side-french; subsequent October operation is corroborated by https://ny.eater.com/maps/best-new-nyc-restaurants-heatmap.

items.title: Altbau brings freshly milled grain breads to Williamsburg
items.summary: The bakery from Tartine co-founder Chad Robertson features on-site milling and pastries by Wei Si Phua. A country loaf or laminated pastry makes a lower-cost way to try a notable opening.
items.price_text: Country loaf $12, reported by The Infatuation on November 3; other prices unknown.
items.conditions: Selection depends on availability. Proposed longer evening hours are not treated as current service. Holiday exceptions are unconfirmed.
items.verification_note: Eater's Brooklyn entry confirms an October opening, on-site milling and pastries by Wei Si Phua, but not the exact day. The November 3 review confirms the $12 country loaf; the official homepage confirms Wednesday–Sunday, 9am until sellout. Sources: https://ny.eater.com/maps/best-new-restaurants-brooklyn-heatmap, https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/altbau-bakery and https://altbaubakery.com/.

items.title: SSRP brings tonkotsu and mazemen to Prospect Heights
items.summary: An October opening serving tonkotsu ramen and mazemen, with sandos and Nagoya-style fried wings broadening the meal beyond noodles.

items.title: One Bryant Park's harvest-themed kaiseki menus
items.address: 135 West 42nd Street, New York, NY 10036, at One Bryant Park
items.summary: Opened in October, the restaurant combines Japanese ingredients and French techniques in five- and eleven-course Niinamesai harvest menus.
items.conditions: The five-course menu lists lobster +$22 and abalone +$38 among opening-course options. The eleven-course menu offers Maine lobster in place of eel for +$26. Menus may vary daily with seasonal availability. Tax, gratuity, service charges, booking requirements and holiday closures are unconfirmed.

items.title: The Otter's daily cocktail hour: $3 oysters, $7 sliders and $11 spritzes

items.title: Ramro's $99 Saturday tasting menu
items.summary: The restaurant's own tasting page specifies six courses served throughout the restaurant, not solely at the counter. The actual dishes change weekly.
items.schedule: Saturdays at 6pm and 8:30pm; not offered Sunday, November 15
items.conditions: Disclose allergies and dietary restrictions when reserving; accommodations are not guaranteed, and same-day adjustments are unavailable without advance notice. items.title: Dirt Candy's five-course vegetarian tasting
items.summary: A fixed-price vegetarian dinner with additional small bites offers a meat-free celebration option. The restaurant confirms that every dish can be made vegan, but gluten-free dinner accommodations are unavailable.
items.price_text: $110 tasting menu; optional wine pairing $55, reported by The Infatuation on November 8, 2026
items.schedule: Tuesday–Saturday, 5:30–10:30pm; closed Sunday and Monday, so not a November 15 dining option
items.conditions: Official policy: no tipping; credit card required for reservations; cancel at least 24 hours ahead to avoid a $50-per-person cancellation fee. Other allergies require advance notice and may not be accommodated. Tax treatment and holiday exceptions unconfirmed.
items.verification_note: The November 8 restaurant-specific editorial entry supplies the $110 tasting and $55 wine pairing. The official FAQ confirms five courses, vegan adaptations, no gluten-free dinner accommodation, no tipping, the credit-card reservation policy and the $50-per-person late-cancellation fee. Its footer confirms Tuesday–Saturday 5:30–10:30pm dinner. No discount is established. Sources: https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/most-affordable-tasting-menu-nyc and https://www.dirtcandynyc.com/faq.
